newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends $6 higher as bulls resurface.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends $6 higher as bulls resurface.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended sharply higher on Tuesday after some bullish traders shrugged off a closed arbitrage to the United States and described the market as cheap following Monday's selloff.
Talk of refinery run cuts in Northwest Europe and a rebound in crude and gasoline futures also helped.
Another factor, they said, was the sharply higher naphtha prices that have discouraged refiners from buying it as a feedstock to make gasoline. Gasoline prices are below naphtha.
"I think gasoline looks pretty good for Europe...I just don't see much around," one trader said.
"Run cuts are always supportive for products...It should be bullish," he added.
But others cautioned that, notwithstanding the volatile crude market, supplies would end up swamping the NWE barge market if the arb stayed shut for long.
Eurograde barges ended $6 higher at $209/$211 fob ARA with the last deal heard done at $210 for 1,000 tonnes. Reguar unleaded closed $5 higher at $203/$205.
Euroilstock said European Union gasoline stocks jumped 8.16 million barrels in January to 164.60 million, but were still 5.6 million below a year ago.
Oil traders said earlier on Tuesday that an estimated 100,000 barrels per day of crude throughput was being cut at European refineries due to poor margins.
British Petroleum said margins at its refineries in January were "very disappointing" and that some business managers were considering cutting throughput.

In the Med, supplies were also snug with no spot cargoes available for the rest of February and some demand for low octane and middle octane material coming from Africa, a trader said. The arb to the U.S. was shut.
A bid for leaded material was heard at $212 fob on Tuesday, but the market was likely closer to $210, the trader said. That would put premium unleaded near $213/$214.
"In the Med, nothing is available for the rest of February," the trader said. "If cargoes are available, we do see opportunities to go outside the Med."
